title: Sell Mineral Rights in Reserve, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Reserve, MT
metaDescription: Reserve, MT sits near the Saskatchewan border in far northern Sheridan County, quiet ground on the Bakken's northern flank. I buy interests here honestly.
heroLead: Reserve sits up near the Saskatchewan line, about as far north as Sheridan County reaches, and the mineral record here is as quiet as the drive up to it.
intro: The Bakken does extend north across the border into Saskatchewan, which surprises some Reserve-area families who assume the play stops at the international line. It doesn't, geologically, but the economics on this side of the border in far northern Sheridan County have never supported the kind of development seen closer to the North Dakota core. Most interests I run into near Reserve are quiet, unleased, homestead-era holdings, and I evaluate them as exactly that.
I mention the Saskatchewan extension because it's genuinely interesting geology, not because it changes what I can offer for ground on this side of the line today.

sections.heading: Basin edge meets international edge
paragraphs: Reserve sits at a genuine double edge — the western flank of the Bakken and the northern edge of the play near the border. Both factors point the same direction: thinner pay, less drilling incentive, and a quieter lease history than counties further south and east. I don't dress that up when I talk to a family here.

sections.heading: What I confirm regardless
paragraphs: Quiet doesn't mean I skip the work. I pull the recorded chain from the Sheridan County Clerk and Recorder in Plentywood, confirm the legal description, and check for any lease history before discussing a number.

sections.heading: What a fair offer on quiet ground looks like
paragraphs: I price interests like this as long-term potential, tied to the broader basin trend rather than to any specific well or unit. It's a smaller number than an active interest would command, and I explain exactly why before you decide anything.

faqs.question: Does the Bakken really reach up near Reserve?
faqs.answer: Geologically it extends north into Saskatchewan, but drilling economics on the Montana side here have never supported significant development. I price interests against that reality.

faqs.question: Is a quiet, unleased interest near Reserve still worth calling about?
faqs.answer: Yes, priced as long-term potential rather than current income. I'll explain that clearly before making an offer.

faqs.question: How do you confirm ownership this far out?
faqs.answer: The same way as anywhere in the county — through the recorded deed chain at the Sheridan County Clerk and Recorder in Plentywood.

faqs.question: Does the international border complicate the title work at all?
faqs.answer: No, the border doesn't affect ownership records on the Montana side. I still work exclusively through Sheridan County and Montana state records.

faqs.question: How do you price ground this far from any active development?
faqs.answer: As long-term potential tied to the broader basin trend, not current income. I walk through that reasoning clearly before making an offer.
